results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 56 outline summaries match the controlling idea of the aligned spec paragraph, in spec order (p01-p56, including p17a). Weakest match is 'Comparing the Case... ¶1' ('Lead-in to the pattern comparison table') against p51, whose verdict on which patterns are supported is carried by the table rather than the prose; see the evidence_is_explained failure.
The reverse outliner marked no unit as holding two ideas.

Every unit ties to a supporting claim: reading rules and evidence limits to V1, regulators, multi-homing and the national table to V2, valuation/Ultimmo/private sellers/commission share to V3, the 2021 intent and 2025 reversal to V4, the rules, comparison, questions and closing to V5.

results.draft_locus: Comparing the Case to the Book's Patterns and to Veldmark ¶1
results.quote: My rules rest on that record, and that record tests the book's patterns as follows:
results.finding: The patterns table is introduced only with 'as follows:' and no sentence before or after it says what it shows. The spec's controlling idea for p51 (the record supports the real-estate, valuation, feed-contract and funnel-metric claims and is only consistent with the multi-country and consolidation claims) is left entirely to the table; the next unit turns straight to Veldmark. Both flow readers also stumbled on this lead-in.

Other evidence is explained: the timeline is framed by its dating rule and Figure 1; regulator decisions are read in Phase 1 ¶6; the 2008 method, 2019 purchase and Figure 3 are tied together in Phase 2 ¶3; the 6% figure is marked self-reported; Ultimmo's features are read in ¶8; the national, asset-type, trade-off and evidence-gap tables each have a sentence stating what they show; Hearthly figures are read as 'France is measured; Spain is not'.

results.quote: By asset type, the record shows a real-estate group with one horizontal asset, and its asset types behaved differently.
results.finding: Declared elaboration carrying over 'the record read by national dimension, ending in a shared core and a local edge'. The opening does not pick up the national reading (the spec's 'rather than by country' is missing), so the shift to a second cut of the same record is not expressed, and the sentence joins two claims; both flow readers re-read it.

results.quote: Together these readings show options that are not a ladder: none is a later stage of another.
results.finding: Declared conclusion_summary carrying over 'the record read by country and by asset type'. 'These readings' does not name the two cuts it summarizes, and 'options' arrives before they are introduced; both flow readers could not tell what 'these readings' meant until after the table.

results.quote: 1. For each capability we plan to share across countries, is it a method, an engine or a product, and does it pass a written clear-advantage test?
results.finding: Declared a word-level elaboration at the start of the section, carrying over 'a decision record that states the shared and local layers'. The section opens directly on the numbered list with no transitional word or lead-in, so the link from the worked decision record to the reader's own questions is left to the heading.

All other transition_in entries (p02-p04, p06-p08, p12-p17a, p19-p27, p29-p30, p32-p35, p37-p38, p40, p44, p46-p50, p52-p53, p56 and the section-level ones for how-to-read, timeline, the four phases, resists, failure-modes, evidence-stops, chief-architect, comparison and the conclusion) express the declared relationship at the boundary and pick up the declared known information. Phase 3's opening expresses the time relationship but obscures the overlap (see flow_is_followable).

results.quote: The book's research checked a claim that Immowelt and Immonet merged in 2023: they were combined as companies in **2015**, not in 2023.
results.finding: Reader A (item 2): the correction 'answers a question nobody asked' and repeats the paragraph above it after the inference callout. Reader B (item 3) the same, and both propose folding it into the 2015 facts or the paragraph above. The difficulty comes from the spec: p17a prescribes a separate refutation of a claim the reader never meets, placed after p17 and its callout, with evidence (both brands run by AVIV Germany in February 2024) that duplicates p17's.

results.quote: The integration phase began in 2021, during the French funnel, and is documented almost entirely by statements of intent.
results.finding: Reader A (item 3): the jump back from 2023 to 2021 made them pause, and 'during the French funnel' reads like a place, not a period. Reader B (item 5): had to re-check the heading dates; the overlap is explained only after the reader is surprised. The spec's order (by start of strand) is sound and its transition says 'set in 2021 while that funnel was being built'; the prose compresses it into an odd time marker.

results.quote: The trade report names KKR, not AVIV, as the seller and says KKR gained full control of Yad2 in March 2025 through the carve-out
results.finding: Reader A (item 4): learning mid-paragraph that the seller may not be AVIV unsettles the 'first visible portfolio move' claim. Reader B (item 6): re-read to work out whose move it was. The spec frames it as the new owners' move; the prose does not make plain that 'the new owners' are KKR acting as seller.

results.quote: the dated January 2025 report in the timeline records two of the 2025 deals, majority stakes in tax-depreciation services
results.finding: Reader A (item 5): a very long sentence; had to go back to the timeline to see which two deals were meant. Reader B (item 7): re-read and still unsure which two of the three are meant. The reconciliation is prose-level clutter, not required by the spec's order.

results.quote: By asset type, the record shows a real-estate group with one horizontal asset, and its asset types behaved differently.
results.finding: Reader A (item 6): awkward, read twice, two claims, ambiguous 'its asset types'. Reader B (item 9): joins two claims awkwardly, read twice, weak link to the previous section. The spec's placement is fine; the sentence obscures it.

results.quote: That is the same neutrality problem the final comparison takes up for Veldmark's Keybridge, its agent software that also feeds Hearthly's competitors
results.finding: Reader A (item 7): a forward reference to a fictional product not yet met pulls the reader out of the AVIV analysis. Reader B (item 9): a forward reference that cannot be fully understood here. Both note the How to Read warning. The spec prescribes this pointer by name (p40 transition introduces 'the same problem for Veldmark's Keybridge', and p08 announces it), so the fault lies in the spec's content.

results.quote: Together these readings show options that are not a ladder: none is a later stage of another.
results.finding: Reader A (item 8): 'these readings' is vague and 'options' appear before the reader knows them. Reader B (item 10): had to read the table first and come back. The order is sound; the opening sentence obscures it.

results.draft_locus: Comparing the Case to the Book's Patterns and to Veldmark ¶1
results.quote: My rules rest on that record, and that record tests the book's patterns as follows:
results.finding: Reader A (item 9): the double 'that record' points back across the whole Chief Architect section, a weak transition. Reader B (item 11): vague, re-read to see it meant AVIV's record. Prose problem.

results.draft_locus: Comparing the Case to the Book's Patterns and to Veldmark ¶2
results.quote: The comparison sharpens four choices: Supply Contract v1, the group's ingestion contract; where Hearthly's search runs; how Valuo's seller leads are sold; and the neutrality of Keybridge

results.draft_locus: From AVIV to the Property Portals ¶1
results.quote: The 2021 goal and the 2025 shift are that boundary announced without a written scope, then corrected.
results.finding: Reader A (item 11): compressed metaphor, second read; the goal and shift 'are' the boundary. Reader B (item 13): re-read; clear only with the next sentence. The spec's synthesis is clear ('that boundary first announced without a written scope and then corrected in an interview'); the prose compresses it.

results.quote: It ends with my decision rules, a comparison with the book's patterns and with Veldmark that applies the same boundary to Hearthly, Veldmark's property portal in France and Spain, questions and a closing.
results.finding: Reader A only (item 1): long sentence with an ambiguous list; re-read to see where the Veldmark clause ends. Minor.

results.quote: AVIV's documented strategy measures supply acquisition (sellers identified, seller leads, commission share) rather than listing counts, which is the cure for this pattern in a vertical where portals earn from leads.
results.finding: Reader B only (item 1): comes before the strategy is met, and the box's logic switches from patterns AVIV shows to one it cures. (The intro reader was also unsure, but is not a flow reader.) Minor.

results.quote: still operating side by side nine years after their 2015 combination
results.finding: Reader B only (item 2): had to work out that nine years after 2015 means 2024, and 'over nine years' just before refers to a different span. Minor.

results.quote: a French or German portal does not own its supply
results.finding: Reader B only (item 4): only the French decision was about multi-homing; extending the point to Germany sent the reader back to the Bundeskartellamt paragraph. The spec prescribes this: p16's controlling idea names French and German portals and its transition carries 'agencies that multi-home, as both regulators describe', while p14 is about network effects, not multi-homing. Minor.

results.quote: Under owners who had just signed a separate sale of Yad2, separable businesses are worth more
results.finding: Reader B only (item 8): the sale was signed the same month as the interview, so 'had just signed' made the reader check whether the reversal came before or after the sale. Minor.

results.quote: The following questions matter to an architect and are not answered by any public source found for this book.
results.finding: Reader B only (part 2 and part 4): the reason this section comes after Trade-offs and Failure Modes rather than before them is unclear; it proposes moving it ahead of them. Reader A found the placement sensible. The position is the spec's (flow rationale: evidence limits close the cross-phase group). Minor.

Both readers describe the organising principle the spec declares: reading rules and timeline, a chronological middle of four phases, cross-phase groupings, then the author's rules, comparison, questions and closing; both found the large-scale order easy to follow. The failed results above are the local points they reported.

Terms on audience.does_not_know are given at or before first use: the brands in the introduction, the mandate glossed in Phase 1 ¶6, notary records in Phase 2 ¶2, DVF in the Veldmark paragraph, OpenImmo as 'a German standard'. Book terms (multi-home, adjacencies, Hearthly, Keybridge, Valuo, Supply Contract v1) are glossed at first use. No flow reader reported an unexplained term; their difficulties were name density and references, recorded under flow_is_followable.

The introduction opens on an intriguing example (portals bought one at a time and then given a European goal), states the question and thesis, and gives a roadmap; none of placeholder, restated question, dictionary, 'dawn of man' or book report.
The conclusion does not open with 'in conclusion', adds no new evidence or subtopic, and does not end on a restated thesis alone: it synthesizes and hands off to the next case.

From AVIV ¶1 states what no single section states (one boundary seen in what was shared and in how the goal changed) and answers the so-what: a group that writes the boundary down layer by layer before staffing can move it later without a write-off.
From AVIV ¶1 returns to the hook ('those portals, bought one at a time') and says which parts were shared and which stayed national, as callback.how requires.

The intro reader named the single question (how much of a property portal can be shared across countries), thin corporate evidence (corporate history, regulators, trade-press interviews, product announcements, no engineering material), the national layers that stop a group platform short of the product, and a comparison applying the boundary to Veldmark's Hearthly; it predicted the roadmap's order (rules, timeline, four phases, cross-phase views, rules, comparison, questions, closing) and the cautious tone. Its open points are about detail, not about the chapter's questions or ending.

The cold reader gave the August 2021 CEO quote and its missing scope, Mseka's December 2025 local autonomy with group functions 'where they create clear advantages', shared infrastructure, data, identity tooling, engines and valuation/ranking methods, local feed adapters, disclosure validation, professional products and lead routing, and a decision record stating shared and local layers, markets per stage, an exit criterion per stage and the evidence that would change the split. Matches expected.

results.finding: Rubric item 1, confirmed: company facts (segment status, Axel Springer's 2020 delisting) with no source in the sentence; the trade-press citation in the next sentence covers only 'does not publish'.

results.quote: Immoweb was a family-founded Belgian portal from 1996; Immowelt and Immonet were Germany's second and third portals; Logic-Immo came with print magazines; Yad2 was Israel's horizontal classifieds leader
results.finding: Rubric item 2, confirmed: the 1996 founding, 'came with print magazines' and 'Israel's horizontal classifieds leader' carry no source; only the German ranking is covered (Bundeskartellamt 2015).

results.quote: AVIV's portals were bought as national leaders and challengers, and their value came from local agent relationships, local data and local monetization.
results.finding: Rubric item 5, confirmed: the author's interpretation stated as fact with no 'my reading' label; the same reading is correctly labeled in Phase 1 ¶2.

results.quote: it never fitted a European real-estate platform
results.finding: Rubric item 9, confirmed: an unlabeled judgement appended to sourced facts; the expected answer requires interpretation to be marked 'my reading'.

results.draft_locus: Why Real Estate Resists One Platform ¶1
results.quote: National supply software, ingestion standards, disclosures, monetization and property data explain AVIV's record, and they are documented outside AVIV.
results.finding: Rubric item 10, confirmed: a causal claim about why AVIV's record looks as it does, stated as fact although AVIV never stated its reasons; it needs the 'my reading' label (the national factors themselves are documented, the explanation of AVIV is not).

Not upheld from the rubric reader: items 3, 4 and 7 are table cells not visible in units.json, and the table note in Why Real Estate ¶2 explicitly labels the judgement entries; item 6 ('each bringing its own technology') and item 8 (the funnel metrics, sourced in Phase 2) are summary statements of facts the body documents. The Phase 2-4 narrative cites each executive statement with publication and year.

results.quote: A goal such as "one European marketplace" can mean anything from shared cloud accounts to one listing service.
results.finding: Rubric Q2 point, confirmed: a paraphrase of AVIV's 2021 goal is set in quotation marks, so it reads as a quotation of the CEO's goal although his words were '...to create a European real estate marketplace'. Drop the quotation marks or use the exact phrase.

The 2021 CEO line is quoted exactly in KEY POINTS, the timeline and Phase 3; 'unified' is not used; 'fully integrated platform' is attributed to the interviewer in the failure-patterns box, the timeline, 'What was not said' and Phase 4 ('The interviewer's question records the reversal'). KEY POINTS' 'the press described' is dated and not presented as AVIV's wording.
